why: The expert projection is 15.4% of the step and had only ever been bounded by reasoning. The driver that answers it existed in the evidence bundle but was never run - its own title says "written, not run".

identities_pinned_and_verified_before_th.note: the first library found on the box was the v1-n64 build (c896289f) and was rejected by the hash guard; the lane pins v2-n64 at 7dce3e3d, which is what these numbers describe

finding_1_the_call_is_dominated_by_per_c.reading: five more experts add only about 110 us, so the call is dominated by per-call cost rather than per-expert bytes. Six groups reach 39.8 GB/s, reproducing the ~38 GB/s the earlier note recorded.

finding_2_practical_reference.which_to_use: the copy reference is the meaningful practical number. The read-only sum reference reports 5.4 GB/s, which is a reduction over an awkward shape rather than a bandwidth measurement, and must not be read as the device limit.

finding_3_standalone_numbers_are_host_bo.consequence: a 4.7x gap means the standalone loop pays host launch and synchronisation the graph does not, so the 344.5 us implied fixed cost must NOT be read as kernel-internal. The harness cannot separate kernel fixed cost from host launch cost and cannot size the opportunity on its own.

finding_4_sized_in_graph_instead.why_that_best_case_is_unreachable: the kernel runs M=1 - one activation row broadcast across expert groups - while the cube unit is built for M=16 tiles, so most of every loaded tile is padding. That is a property of single-request decode, not of this implementation, and it is the same reason a larger acceptance length is so much faster.

conclusion: The item is real, but its honest in-graph size is about 2.4x off a practical copy reference, not the order of magnitude the raw fixed-cost line implies. The dominant cause is M=1 tile padding, which a better kernel cannot remove without more tokens per step. This closes "swap the LUT kernel" as a route to 50 tok/s, while leaving room for perhaps 1 to 2 ms from a better M=1 kernel.
method: the driver shipped in the evidence bundle, run for the first time, both pinned hashes verified before the run; single card, no model, no checkpoint or CANN change
